Package neqsim.process.safety.selfheating

Class PorousMediaSelfHeatingAnalyzer

java.lang.Object
neqsim.process.safety.selfheating.PorousMediaSelfHeatingAnalyzer
public class PorousMediaSelfHeatingAnalyzer extends Object
Frank-Kamenetskii steady-state criticality screening for self-heating in a reactive porous body.

Solves the classical thermal-explosion question for a body that generates heat internally by a slow exothermic reaction and loses it by conduction to its boundary: does a stable steady-state temperature profile exist, or must the body run away to ignition? This is the governing question for lagging fires, where a combustible liquid has soaked into porous thermal insulation.

The steady-state energy balance with an Arrhenius volumetric source

lambda * grad^2(T) + P * exp(-E / (R * T)) = 0

is reduced by the Frank-Kamenetskii exponential approximation about the boundary temperature to a single dimensionless group

delta = (E * P * r^2) / (lambda * R * Ta^2) * exp(-E / (R * Ta))

where P = A * Q * rho is the volumetric heat-release pre-exponential factor [W/m3], E the activation energy [J/mol], r the characteristic half-dimension [m], lambda the effective thermal conductivity of the wetted porous medium [W/(m K)] and Ta the boundary temperature [K]. A steady state exists only while delta <= deltaCrit, where deltaCrit depends only on the body shape (see SelfHeatingGeometry).

Because delta scales with r^2, doubling the insulation thickness quadruples the criticality parameter. This size dependence is the reason a sample that is perfectly stable in a laboratory dish can ignite when the same material is applied as a thick layer, and it is why a lumped adiabatic screening such as RunawayReactionAnalyzer cannot answer this question.

The kinetic inputs E and P are not obtainable from equilibrium thermodynamics and must come from hot-storage (basket) testing; see BasketTestRegression.

Usage example: 

 PorousMediaSelfHeatingAnalyzer analyzer = new PorousMediaSelfHeatingAnalyzer();
 analyzer.setGeometry(SelfHeatingGeometry.SLAB);
 analyzer.setCharacteristicDimension(50.0, "mm");
 analyzer.setEffectiveThermalConductivity(0.09);
 analyzer.setActivationEnergy(110.0, "kJ/mol");
 analyzer.setVolumetricHeatReleasePreFactor(2.5e12);
 analyzer.setBoundaryTemperature(180.0, "C");
 PorousMediaSelfHeatingResult result = analyzer.analyze();

References: Frank-Kamenetskii, Diffusion and Heat Transfer in Chemical Kinetics, 2nd ed.; Bowes, Self-Heating: Evaluating and Controlling the Hazards, 1984; Babrauskas, Ignition Handbook, 2003.

    • forPipeInsulation

      public PorousMediaSelfHeatingAnalyzer forPipeInsulation(double insulationThickness, String thicknessUnit, double pipeWallTemperature, String temperatureUnit)
      Configure the analyzer for a layer of liquid-wetted insulation on a hot pipe or vessel wall.

      The layer is treated as an infinite slab whose characteristic half-dimension equals the full insulation thickness and whose boundary temperature equals the pipe wall temperature. This is deliberately conservative: the hot process surface supplies heat rather than removing it, so the pipe-side face behaves as an adiabatic symmetry plane, and taking the whole layer at the pipe wall temperature bounds the real profile, which falls towards ambient at the outer face. A case that screens as SelfHeatingVerdict.SUBCRITICAL on this basis is safe; a case that screens as SelfHeatingVerdict.SELF_IGNITION should be refined with SelfHeatingInductionSolver using the true boundary temperatures before any decision is taken.

      Parameters:
      insulationThickness - insulation layer thickness; must be positive
      thicknessUnit - length unit of the thickness ("m", "cm", "mm" or "in")
      pipeWallTemperature - process-side wall temperature
      temperatureUnit - temperature unit ("K" or "C")
      Returns:
      this analyzer for chaining
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if the thickness is not positive or a unit is unsupported

    • criticalityParameter

      private double criticalityParameter(double boundaryTemperature, double dimension)
      Evaluate the Frank-Kamenetskii criticality parameter at a given boundary temperature and body size.

      Evaluated in logarithmic form to avoid overflow of the Arrhenius term at low temperature.

      Parameters:
      boundaryTemperature - boundary temperature [K]; must be positive
      dimension - characteristic half-dimension [m]; must be positive
      Returns:
      the dimensionless criticality parameter delta

    • solveCriticalTemperature

      private double solveCriticalTemperature(double dimension, double deltaCrit)
      Solve for the boundary temperature at which delta equals its critical value for a fixed body size.

      Delta increases monotonically with temperature over the physically relevant range, so a simple bisection is robust.

      Parameters:
      dimension - characteristic half-dimension [m]; must be positive
      deltaCrit - critical Frank-Kamenetskii parameter for the shape
      Returns:
      the critical boundary temperature [K], or Double.NaN if it cannot be bracketed
